MultiDock — a dock on every monitor
====================================

INSTALL (about a minute)

1. Drag MultiDock into the Applications folder (right here in this window).

2. Open Applications and double-click MultiDock.
   macOS will say it "could not verify" MultiDock. That's normal: it's a
   homemade app, not one from the App Store. Click Done.

3. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to the
   "Security" section, and click "Open Anyway" next to MultiDock.
   Enter your password, then click Open Anyway again.

   You only have to do this once.

4. The MultiDock Settings window opens. Click a display, pick where its
   dock goes, and choose its apps. Done!


USING IT

- MultiDock lives in the menu bar (the little dock icon at the top of the
  screen). Use it to open Settings, turn on Auto-hide, or quit.
- Out of the box it shows a dock on every display EXCEPT the one that already
  has the normal macOS Dock. You can change that in Settings.
- Each display can be on any edge (bottom, left, right, top) and centered or
  in a corner.
- Each display can mirror your normal Dock or have its own custom list of
  apps and folders.
- Right-click any icon for Hide, Quit, "Remove from This Dock", etc.
  Right-click a running app and choose "Keep in This Dock" to add it.
- Drop an app or folder onto an empty part of a dock to add it there.
- Turn on "Launch at login" in Settings so it starts with your Mac.


STEP 3 DIDN'T WORK?

Open Terminal and paste this, then press Return:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/MultiDock.app

Then double-click MultiDock again.


UPDATES

MultiDock checks for new versions on its own and asks before installing.
You can also click "Check for Updates…" in its menu bar menu.


UNINSTALL

Quit MultiDock from its menu bar icon, then drag it from Applications
to the Trash.


Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or newer. Works on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
